Appendix: Class traits

Classes have limited impact on a character’s gameplay during combat or in other forms of gameplay challenges. Resources largely function as a way of a “character class”, determining the style of your gameplay. You can flavor your character’s abilities as any class you wish and there will be no hard limits on class/race combinations (but I may ask questions if you bring up, for example, an undead paladin).

Most character classes will grant you a unique “class trait” which allows you to ignore or change a certain game mechanic, just for this character, listed below.

Class traits can be upgraded with AP, but every upgrade usually requires consultation with the Game Master.

Learning class traits

Most characters will start with one class trait, or on occasion two. Altogether, you can normally learn up to three class traits. Additional class traits beyond the ones you start with can be learned by using the training feature and employing an NPC with the right class, who isn’t otherwise occupied, for a week and 100🪙 , or by asking a fellow player with the class to help.

Developing class traits

If there are no characters, be it player characters or heroic NPCs, in any of the guilds that already possess the specific version of the class trait you want, you may, with the Guild Master’s approval, peruse the service of another NPC and go together to develop the class trait for a week. Paying the NPC 100🪙, at the end of the week both characters will earn the class trait and be able to train others.

Recruiting class trainers

Some class traits may merit actually recruiting an additional NPC that will serve as a class trainer henceforth. To do that, you may take another character familiar with a place you could find such a class trainer, and spend a week looking for the trainer. At the end of the week, a new NPC will appear and be able to train you in the trait. This service does not cost you anything but time.

StarCraft characters

Elements of the StarCraft setting have been adapted into the main WarCraft-based universe, and therefore creation of characters inspired by StarCraft units is possible. A full list of all StarCraft units and their class traits would be too long, but the following general rules apply.

Characters based on Terran or Protoss units may use any class traits from canon WarCraft traits, hero talent traits, WarCraft Earth traits, and custom Warcraft class traits, as adapted to depict a specific unit.

Even lightly armored StarCraft units, such as marines, may use heavy (plate) armor, since the Koprulu Sector’s light armor is much heavier than that of Azeroth. Still, the armor and weapons of both sectors are comparable because it’s an adaptation that uses a more Azeroth-style technology than the hyper-advanced sci-fi of StarCraft.

Terran/Eutopian base classes

Due to the merging of StarCraft and WarCraft universes, Terrans are called “Eutopians”, as descendants of the Arathi who crashed on planet Eutopia instead of the other side of Azeroth (which looks different in this universe).

Despite being in the same universe as main WarCraft characters, Eutopian characters use a different set of base classes.

Inherited base classes (with hero talents): Gunslinger, Medic, Tinker

Terran/Eutopian units

Specific Terran units are treated as equivalent to hero talents or subclasses from other universes. Most can be picked up by any base class.

Terran units and their traits can be trained in specific facilities built by allied companies, without the use of a specific trainer NPC. Otherwise, the training cost and time remain unaffected.

The colors in the unit name field represent the faction that needs to be contacted and recruited before the unit is available. Some unit variants are original.

Witcher characters

Witcher

Weapon

Fuel (mana), Focus (energy)

Typical Pets:

Witcher Mutagens: Witchers can use their bonus action with their alchemy crafting roll (without reroll on failure) to craft and immediately consume a beneficial potion of their choice.

Witchers can drink multiple mutagens, with succeeding bonus actions, but each one increases their toxicity attribute by amount equal to the potion's duration or magnitude (whichever is higher).

When the witcher's toxicity exceeds their health upon drinking the mutagen, they roll an injury roll. Toxicity can be lowered with healing rolls, and the resulting injuries can be cured with first aid.

Special Notes: Witcher class trait takes up two class trait slots. Witchers also gain Witcher Physiology creature type traits, listed in the main document.

Tamriel (Elder Scrolls) characters

Because the original system is not class-based, characters from the Elder Scrolls setting do not gain class traits by default (but can train one later). Instead, they start with a single birthsign trait - a core element of the fantasy. For immersion’s sake, it’s best if the birthsign is selected randomly.

Birthsign traits are exempt from the normal class trait limits, however you can have only one at a time. They cannot normally be “trained”, but to acquire them you have to spend a week and your training slot to venture to an area known for its standing stones on Nirn, pay 100 gold for the trip and ritual ingredients, and choose between one of the three options: a sign related to the current Tamriel month, a sign related to the area, and a randomly selected sign (rerolled once each Tamriel month).

  • The Apprentice: Elfborn: +1 starting mana/magicka.
  • The Atronach: Wombburn: -10 mana recovery, on being targeted with magic, roll 1d3, On 3, +1 magicka.
  • The Lady: Lady’s Grace: +1 starting stamina.
  • The Lord: Blood of the North: Up to three times per day, use a bonus action to perform a HoT roll on yourself.
  • The Lover: Lover's Kiss: Use a bonus action to perform a control roll on another unit and control defense (2) roll on yourself, draining your own fatigue to damage theirs.
  • The Mage: Fay: At the start of combat, you can use your bonus action to buff your mana/magicka until the encounter ends.
  • The Ritual: Blessed Word: allows mental effects on undead as if the character used holy magic, and Mara's Gift: +10 to self-healing
  • The Serpent: Star-Curse: Up to three times per day, touch a hostile creature to poison it, rolling a (poison) DoT on it.
  • The Shadow: Moonshadow: Up to three times per day, use a bonus action to roll stealth/hide.
  • The Steed: Charioteer: Up to three times per day, use a bonus action to roll a buff to your own speed
  • The Thief: Akaviri Danger-Sense: Up to three times per day, use a bonus action to roll a buff to your defense until the encounter ends.
  • The Tower: Tower Key: Once per day, the character may bypass a lock of up to 50 DC.
  • The Warrior: Warwyrd: At the start of combat, you can use your bonus action to buff your attack until the encounter ends.

Thedas (Dragon Age) characters

Class traits of Dragon Age characters are assigned per specialization rather than class (which are very limited in number in the original games). If the specialization has an equivalent Warcraft class and is not mentioned below, it uses the same class trait. For the purpose of mission table counters, all specializations count as their parent class unless otherwise specified.

Magic: the Gathering characters

Characters from one of the planes of the MtG multiverse are not too tied to typical character classes. Instead, their playstyle depends on the mana colors they use primarily.

Characters who start with two mana colors trained can pick up two of the following class traits:

  • Black: Sacrifice: Black mana users can use their own health as a resource.
  • Blue: Counterplay: Blue mana users can interrupt multiple times per round.
  • Green: Mana Ramp: Green mana users regenerate +1 mana every turn when not using mana.
  • Red: First Strike: Red mana users can use hostile bonus actions during scamper.
  • White: Divine Protection: can sacrifice their offensive round to gain invulnerability for the defensive round without invoking forbearance.
  • Colorless: Devoid: The colorless mana user can once per day pick one of the other mana color traits, keeping that knowledge for the day.
  • Phyrexian: Sacrifice: Phyrexian mana users can use their own health as a resource.
  • Snow: Chill: Your actions do not trigger reactions.

Characters who start with just one mana color trained can pick up an additional trait for their color:

  • Black: Lifelink: During any round you attacked, you regenerate +1 health.
  • Blue: Evasion: You cannot be taunted, charmed, misdirected, or otherwise manipulated to be unable to target a specific unit unless you lose control of your character.
  • Green: Regeneration: Regenerates +1 health every turn when not attacked or suffering from a DoT.
  • Red: Double Strike: Sole red mana users can use 1 mana to gain a bonus action to repeat their main action.
  • White: Vigilance: Sole white mana users can tank for others multiple times per round.
  • Colorless: Flexibility: The colorless mana user may once per day choose to copy another party character's class trait, keeping that knowledge for the day.
  • Phyrexian: Infect: Using a bonus action with your attacks, you can turn any damage to health into health debuff (for 3 rounds).

The list above is a work in progress, updated as need arises.

You are allowed to bring up a more unusual concept if you can explain how it works within the confines of our combined lore.

There are no hard limits on multi-classing, so you can describe your character as a mage/warlock or a rogue/hunter. Once again, I may ask questions if you bring up specific strange combinations such as paladin/death knights or death knight/demon hunters. A multi-classing character may gain one or more of their class traits if they spend AP on traits related to their constituent classes.
